answer: For a poll on a grove in a dune hollow, a registrar checks photo IDs against a registry and blind-signs one election-bound token per matching, unused ID; mismatches and repeats are refused. The server verifies the signature and election binding, accepting each token once and rejecting invalid or reused tokens. Extra tokens require more accepted IDs and visits, potentially costing recruitment effort. Borrowed IDs enable abuse, and people without accepted IDs are excluded.
